Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking the time during the product call today. As we evaluate Redwood for our pilot, our Security & Privacy team needs a few concrete answers about where customer data is processed and how deletion is enforced. Can you confirm the following for Novus Health?

1) Primary processing regions: For requests pinned to EU residency, which cloud regions and data centers can actually execute inference for our tenant? Please list cloud regions (by major provider/region code) and whether any EU requests may be routed to non-EU zones as a fallback.

2) Subprocessors: We need a list of third-party subprocessors that touch request or telemetry data (including CDN, monitoring, logging, backups). A simple CSV with service name, role, and region is ideal.

3) Short-term caching / KV cache: Does Redwood persist KV cache or prefix caches to disk in ways that survive instance restarts? If so, how is TTL enforced and how quickly can cached tokens be purged on request?

4) Backups & snapshots: Are model artifacts or request logs backed up to long-term storage? If so, where are those backups located and what is your deletion/retention process when a customer requests complete erasure?

5) Deletion SLA and evidence: If Novus requests deletion of retained inference logs and KV cache snapshots, what is the typical SLA to fully remove data from active and backup stores? What evidence can Redwood provide?

6) Cross-border transfers: Please explain circumstances that would cause EU-pinned traffic to leave the EU (e.g., capacity shortages, disaster recovery), and what contractual/technical controls you put in place (encryption, pseudonymization, access restrictions).

If you can attach your regional subprocessor matrix and a short deletion playbook, that would help speed our procurement review.

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear list. Answers below at a high level; I attached a regional subprocessor matrix (CSV) and a short deletion playbook (PDF) per your request. If you need more formal evidence (SOC2 report) I can loop in our security team and share the summary under an NDA.

1) Primary processing regions
- EU-residency option: We run inference in EU-GCP (europe-west4), EU-Azure (westeurope), and EU-AWS (eu-west-1) depending on customer configuration and availability.
- Routing policy: For customers pinning to EU, requests are routed to EU execution pools. We only route outside the EU in constrained scenarios (see section 6).

2) Subprocessors
- Attached CSV lists active subprocessors by role (edge CDN, monitoring, log storage, model registry) and the regions where they operate. Key examples: FastEdge CDN (edge caching, global), MetricSight (observability, EU+US), CloudStore (persistent snapshots, EU/US depending on bucket config).

3) KV/prefix cache behavior
- KV cache is in-memory by default. We persist warm caches to local NVMe for faster warm starts; persisted cache files have explicit TTLs and are encrypted at rest. On a customer delete request we mark the tenant's cache stripe for immediate eviction; in practice eviction from active servers is immediate (seconds-minutes) and persisted cache blobs are removed within the deletion SLA (see below).

4) Backups & snapshots
- Operational snapshots (debug logs, model artifacts) are taken for operational integrity. Backups for EU-pinned tenants can be configured to use EU-only buckets. If you select our EU-only residency option during onboarding, backups are placed in EU regions and marked with EU-only access controls.

5) Deletion SLA and evidence
- Typical SLA: 30 days for full purge from active services and nearline snapshots; 90 days for cold backups (unless otherwise negotiated in a contract).
- Evidence: We can provide a deletion certificate (signed), audit log entries showing deletion operations, and (subject to contract/NDA) a redacted cloud delete job history.

6) Cross-border transfer controls
- Fallback scenarios: We may temporarily route to non-EU pools for brief periods if EU capacity is exhausted and the customer has allowed burst-to-global in their config.
- Controls: data-in-transit encryption, per-tenant KMS with regional key controls, and policy-based routing that prioritizes EU pools. For contracts that disallow any cross-border transfers, we can enforce strict region pinning; this may affect burst capacity and latency.

Hi Amelia — quick answers below and I've looped in Marissa (Customer Success) and Dev (Security) to provide any deeper artifacts.

- NVMe snapshots and backup replication: For EU-only tenants we do not replicate NVMe local cache snapshots to non-EU buckets by default. Local persisted cache files are used for warm starts and are encrypted; when a customer requests deletion we run a targeted cache purge job that removes local files and then issues a delete to any nearline object stores. Operational backups (if enabled for your account) are stored in region-specific buckets; cross-region replication is off for EU-only configs unless explicit consent is granted.

- Pseudonymization prior to cross-border routing: By default we do not transform request payloads before routing. If you require pseudonymization, we offer an optional preprocessing hook (de-identification step) that can run in-region before any outbound routing or be applied via customer-side SDKs. Contractual protections: we support SCCs and will put explicit contractual clauses to forbid routing without SCCs or customer consent.

- SOC2 scope summary: Dev: can you confirm the latest SOC2 type II kit and the covered services/test period? We will share the summary under NDA.

1) I'll attach a redlined SOC2 summary (high level) once Dev confirms — we will need your signed NDA to share the full report.
2) Schedule a 30-minute session next Tue/Wed for a technical walkthrough (Marissa to coordinate).
